spans.operation: read in the raw player-referee dyad dataset from CSV as the analysis population
average the two independent raters' scores into a single continuous skin_tone measure
bin the continuous skin_tone score into light (0.00-0.25) vs dark (0.75-1.00) categories, leaving the 0.25-0.75 middle range as missing/excluded
collapse the red-card count into a binary any-red-card indicator per dyad
drop dyads with missing or middle-range skin tone, keeping only the two extreme categories for analysis
collapse free-text position strings into broad role buckets (Goalkeeper/Defender/Midfielder/Forward/Other/Missing) via keyword matching
restrict the sample to complete cases on height, weight, and position category, dropping the rest
compute and report the crude, unadjusted red-card rate difference and odds ratio between dark- and light-skinned players as a pre-adjustment benchmark
z-standardize the continuous covariates (height, weight, games, goals) before entering them into the regression
one-hot encode position category and league country, dropping the first level as reference
choose which covariates make up the adjustment set entering the regression models
cluster standard errors by player to account for repeated dyads contributed by the same player
choose a linear probability model (OLS) as the primary specification for estimating the risk difference
choose a logistic regression as the secondary specification for estimating the odds ratio
rescale the risk-difference coefficient and CI from a proportion to percentage points for reporting
exponentiate the logit coefficient and CI to report an odds ratio rather than a log-odds scale
approximate standard errors/confidence intervals for the descriptive plot panels using a normal (Wald) approximation on the binomial rates and log-odds ratio
apply a two-sided alpha=0.05 significance threshold together with the sign of the CI to decide whether the hypothesis is supported, contradicted, or undetermined
